svg.text: INDIAN DRAINAGE SYSTEMS: HIMALAYAN VS PENINSULAR
Comparative Hydrography, Major Basins, Flow Directions & Tributaries

g.text: HIMALAYAN DRAINAGE SYSTEM
• Perennial Nature: Fed by both rainfall & melting snow
• Antecedent Drainage: Pre-date Himalayas; cut deep gorges
• Course: Long youthful courses, meanders, oxbow lakes, floodplains
Three Master Basins:
1. INDUS (2,880 km): Origin near Mansarovar (Bokhar Chu);
Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, Satluj (Panjnad)
2. GANGA (2,525 km): Origin Gangotri (Bhagirathi + Alaknanda at Devprayag);
Left: Ramganga, Gomti, Ghaghara, Gandak, Kosi. Right: Yamuna, Son.
3. BRAHMAPUTRA (2,900 km): Tsangpo in Tibet; Dihang in Arunachal;
Majuli island; Subansiri, Kameng, Manas, Teesta
PENINSULAR DRAINAGE SYSTEM
• Non-Perennial / Ephemeral: Dependent exclusively on monsoon rainfall
• Consequent / Superimposed: Mature, graded profiles, shallow valleys
• Western Ghats act as the principal water divide
East-Flowing (Bay of Bengal — Form Deltas):
• GODAVARI (1,465 km, Dakshin Ganga): Trimbak, Nasik; Penganga, Wainganga
• KRISHNA (1,400 km): Mahabaleshwar; Koyna, Tungabhadra, Bhima
• KAVERI (800 km): Brahmagiri; Shivanasamudra falls; Hemavati, Kabini
• MAHANADI (851 km): Sihawa (Chhattisgarh); Hirakud dam
West-Flowing (Arabian Sea — Form Estuaries, Rift Valleys):
• NARMADA (1,312 km, Amarkantak) & TAPI (724 km, Betul, Multai)
UTTAR PRADESH RIVER NETWORKS & CONFLUENCES:

Prayagraj Sangam (Ganga, Yamuna, mythical Saraswati) • Gomti (origin Fulhar Jheel, Pilibhit, UP) flows through Lucknow, Sultanpur, Jaunpur • Yamuna enters UP at Saharanpur, exits into Ganga at Prayagraj.
